overview: This Senate resolution congratulates the Chicago Cubs baseball team on its 150th anniversary, on August 29, 2026. It recounts the team's history since it became a founding member of baseball's National League in 1876, including its record-tying 116 wins in 1906, its World Series titles in 1907, 1908 and 2016, and its home at Wrigley Field, a National Historic Landmark the team has played in since 1916. It also recognizes famous players and broadcasters and the team's charity work for young people and families. The resolution is a formal statement of praise and does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors a franchise woven into the history of American sports and the life of Chicago, and the pride it has given generations of fans.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and that commending a single private sports team is a minor use of the Senate's time.
